blocks.title: The metanym game
blocks.content:
OUT GROUND TRUTH THAT RISES WITH THE MODELS
IT MEASURES
David Nordfors
david.nordfors@archetypes.ai
ABSTRACT
We introduce a benchmark that is fully self-contained, needs no ground truth, and
rises with the models it measures. Language models compete at making analo-
gies and subjectively grade one another; nothing enters from outside. The bench-
mark reproduces GPQA Diamond, a keyed benchmark of expert-written ques-
tions, at r = 0.98, audited for a leak and found clean. We hypothesize that both
benchmarks measure the same thing in different ways: a language model holds its
knowledge as archet

summary.text: Title tail, author and abstract: 'The Metanym Game: An LLM Benchmark Without Ground Truth That Rises With the Models It Measures' by David Nordfors. Language models compete at writing analogies and grade one another, with nothing from outside; the benchmark reproduces GPQA Diamond at r = 0.98, audited for leaks. A player writes a context template whose slots, filled with keyword sets (metanyms) from different domains, give factually true descriptions; ground truth is replaced by the SVD of the factual rating matrix, which rates players as judges and as generators at once, and subjective criteria are weighted by consistency under a swept calibration anchor. Strong generators were middling judges; a council of the five best issues the ratings, with contestable seats.

blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content:
Nearly every benchmark for machine intelligence needs a predetermined ground truth — golden
keys and labels, oracle models, human panels. The benchmark reported here needs none of that.
It is a game where frontier language models compete in making up analogies and then grade one
another, and that grading is the single source of every score: no human raters, no answer key, nothing
to look up.
The test is the metanym game. A player authors, from nothing, a context template — a paragraph of
fixed wording with open slots — together with the sets of keywords that fill it, each set instantiating
the

summary.text: Introduction: almost every benchmark needs predetermined ground truth; this one is a game where frontier LLMs invent analogies and grade each other, and that grading is the only source of scores. A player writes a context template with open slots plus keyword sets that instantiate it truthfully in different domains; corresponding keywords are metanyms and the instantiations are parallel contexts of one archetypal context (Figure 1). Items written during the run cannot have been trained on, and sentence-by-sentence factual verdicts let one matrix of ratings reveal competent judges without labels, who are then seated as the grading council. The canonical twelve-model run finds judgement is the bottleneck and the key-free total tracks GPQA Diamond at r = 0.98. Lists the contributions and outlines the evaluation pass against a fixed reference pinned at an anchor value.

blocks.title: Participants and protocol
blocks.content:
Twelve frontier LLMs from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI are the participants (named in §4.4),
each simultaneously generator and evaluator. The roster spans an order of magnitude in scale, three
vendors, and adjacent versions within families. All twelve are called with Temperature 0, reason-
ing disabled, tools disabled, so the one greedy response is the measurement. Each model generates
one portfolio — five archetypal contexts, each a template (typically 5–8 sentences, 6–10 slots; the
prompt fixes only the counts, Appendix B) with a metanym table of five domains, 25 instantia-
tions — then eval

summary.text: Participants and protocol: twelve frontier LLMs from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI each generate and evaluate, all at temperature 0 with reasoning and tools disabled. Each writes one portfolio of five archetypal contexts (templates of about 5–8 sentences and 6–10 slots, each instantiated in five domains, 25 instantiations), then scores every other portfolio on the six-axis 1–10 rubric, one anonymised target per call beside a fixed anchor portfolio pinned at 7, giving a 12×11 evaluator-by-generator matrix. Official ratings pool three full runs; the anchor sweep was run once.

blocks.title: The rubric and the anchor
blocks.content:
Three design choices. A fixed anchor: cardinal scores drift between evaluators — one model’s
“8” is another’s “6” — and a reference pinned at a known score turns each idiosyncratic scale into
a common one and recovers discriminability at the top, where the 1–10 ceiling compresses the
strongest portfolios (§4.1). Holistic axes, minimally prescribed: a detailed rubric would leak back

from the anchor submission; its context template, metanym table (one metan

summary.text: The rubric and the anchor: a fixed anchor pinned at a known score turns each evaluator's idiosyncratic scale into a common one and restores discrimination near the ceiling; the axes are holistic and minimally defined so the rubric does not become a template-writing tutorial. Table 1 lists the six axes: factual correctness per parallel context, beauty, intelligence, instantiation distinctness and impressive length per archetype, and structural diversity per portfolio; impressive length counterweights per-sentence factual scoring, which would otherwise reward minimal templates. Includes captions for Figure 1 (a generated archetype, 'Gradient-Guided Navigation') and Figure 2 (the council evaluating one Gemini 2.5 Flash parallel context).

blocks.content: Figure 1 illustrates the context template, metanym keyword table across domains, and instantiated parallel contexts.
Figure 2 displays the five-judge council ratings, rubric axes, and justifications for one context instantiation.

blocks.title: Two key-free estimators
blocks.content:
1. Factual competence — peer centrality. We assume that good evaluators agree with one another
about which instantiations are factually weaker, once each evaluator’s own leniency is removed —
the better two evaluators are, the more they agree. Stack the participants’ factual scores into one
matrix — twelve evaluators against the 275 parallel contexts of the eleven scored portfolios — each
entry the 1–10 rating used directly, row-centre it to remove each evaluator’s leniency, and take its
SVD; the row-centred ˜F (evaluators × instantiations) is well approximated by its leading rank-one
factor,

summary.text: Two key-free estimators. Factual competence by peer centrality: row-centre the 12-evaluator by 275-instantiation factual score matrix to remove leniency and take its SVD; the leading left singular vector gives each judge's competence (eigenvector centrality in the agreement network, rescaled so the anchor reads 7) and the right vector, aggregated, gives generation factuality, a graded relative of Dawid–Skene-style aggregation. Rating consistency by anchor sweep: re-run with the anchor at 5, 6, 7 and 8 and correlate each judge's scores across anchor values per axis, giving an evaluator competence on the subjective axes. Neither can replace the other: agreement only signals truth on facts, and consistency cannot certify truth, so the council is seated on the factual axis with consistency as a bar.

blocks.title: Council, total rating, and scaling by addition
blocks.content:
The council. The council is the five players with the highest total T (eq. 2) and issues every official
rating. The top five are the better factual judges (loadings 0.26–0.61, §4.2); the sixth reads 0.18, and
the line is drawn there.
The total. Each side of the Metanym Game splits into a factual and a criterion half: on generation,
GF (the SVD generation factuality) and GC (the council’s leave-self-out mean over the five non-
factual axes, each seat’s vote weighted by its own consistency on that axis); on evaluation, EF =
7f/fa and EC = 7¯r/¯ra — the anchor model scores 7 on every component. T

summary.text: Council, total and scaling by addition: the council is the five players with the highest total (factual loadings 0.26–0.61; the sixth is 0.18). The total T is the mean of four anchored components, generation factuality, council-rated generation on the non-factual criteria, evaluator factual competence and evaluator consistency, with joint bootstrap intervals. New models are scored against the standing council and anchor; seats are contested by beating the lowest seat's total by a resolvable margin, with two fixed 'ballast' portfolios to keep the factual axis identified and guards on the spectral gap (σ1/σ2 ≥ 2) and the spread of seats' factual scores. Contamination is handled by writing items in the run, archiving fixed material and rejecting copies.

blocks.title: Anchoring doubles resolution
blocks.content:
The bootstrap opens with a raw pass — every portfolio scored by every other model with no anchor,
averaged leave-self-out, 95% bootstrap intervals (2,000 resamples; Efron & Tibshirani, 1993). It
supplies the baseline: the top-ranked portfolio, claude-opus-4.5’s, whose first archetype is Figure
1, is pinned at 7 on every axis, leaving headroom above. Re-run anchored (Appendix G), the gap
between a leading eight and a trailing four more than doubles relative to the spread of the means,
while ranks within either band stay unresolved.
4.2

summary.text: Anchoring doubles resolution: an initial un-anchored pass (leave-self-out means, 2,000-resample bootstrap) picks the top portfolio, claude-opus-4.5's, as the anchor pinned at 7. Re-scored against it, the gap between a leading eight and a trailing four more than doubles relative to the spread of means, though ranks within each band stay unresolved.

blocks.title: The official leaderboard: judgement is the bottleneck
blocks.content:
Every official number is council-issued on the contest basis of §3.4: each model is rated by the five
seats — joined by the model itself when it holds no seat — over the incumbents’ portfolios, the two
ballast submissions and its own, leave-self-out throughout. The two bases agree closely (Spearman
0.98; on the twelve-evaluator basis the fifth seat is a tie within 0.03).
Table 2: Final leaderboard — total T with its joint-bootstrap 95% CI, the evaluator half E, the
generator half G, and the four anchored components; all council-issued against the fixed anchor,
which reads 7.00 by construction.

summary.text: The official leaderboard (Table 2): each model is rated by the five seats on the contest basis, which agrees with the twelve-evaluator basis (Spearman 0.98). Claude Opus 4.5 (the anchor) reads 7.00, then Gemini 3.1 Pro 6.92, Claude Opus 4.1 6.02, Opus 4.0 5.81 and Gemini 2.5 Flash 5.75, down to gpt-4o-mini at 2.39; adjacent ranks are resolved only at 2–3 and 8–9. The top five totals are exactly the five best factual judges. Generating and judging come apart: the Opus models are the strongest generators but middling factual judges (EF 3.5–3.7), while the best judge, Gemini 3.1 Pro (EF 7.78), generates mid-pack, contradicting peer rankers that assume a strong generator is a strong judge.

blocks.title: A key-free benchmark replicates a keyed one
blocks.content:
We test the key-free rating against GPQA Diamond (Rein et al., 2023) — 198 graduate-level
multiple-choice questions written and validated by domain experts — put to the same twelve models
under the same protocol two weeks after the generation run (Appendix D.2), and correlated with T
(Figure 3).
T reproduces GPQA’s ordering at Pearson r = 0.98 [0.95, 0.99] (Spearman 0.96; three runs pooled,
§4.6). Instruments sharing no item authors, task or scoring, and agreeing at 0.98, are as close as
their measurement error allows (Appendix D.1); §6 offers a hypothesis for what they share. Within
the leadi

summary.text: A key-free benchmark replicates a keyed one: GPQA Diamond (198 expert questions) was given to the same twelve models two weeks later, and T reproduces its ordering at Pearson r = 0.98 [0.95, 0.99] (Spearman 0.96), 0.94 within the leading eight. An audit finds no key in any prompt, reproducible accuracies, a balanced key and independent extraction, with strict rescoring moving r by 0.010. Each quarter alone correlates 0.81–0.95, the factual pair 0.94, and only the full total reaches 0.98. Among the leading eight the evaluator factual score is the best single predictor, suggesting judging is a distinct trait no keyed benchmark measures. Captions for Figure 3 (T vs GPQA) and Figure 4 (the shared-archetype hypothesis).

blocks.content: Figure 3 shows scatter plot and linear fit demonstrating r=0.98 agreement between Metanym Game score T and GPQA Diamond.
Figure 4 illustrates the hypothesis that models store archetypal relational structures instantiated into domain metanyms.

blocks.content:

anchor; the main text pools the three. Apart, the runs agree on the total (Appendix F) and track
GPQA at 0.97, 0.97 and 0.92, and most archetype titles recur verbatim between the two runs made

summary.text: Robustness to regeneration: the full pipeline was run three times at temperature 0 against the frozen anchor. The runs agree on the total and track GPQA at 0.97, 0.97 and 0.92, and 34 of 48 archetype titles recur verbatim between runs two hours apart, but the factual quarter is unstable: one seat's EF reads 4.68, 3.81 and 0.01, and run 3's factual axis is unidentified (σ1/σ2 = 1.29). Single-run re-selection would rotate one seat in runs 2 and 3, neither passing the guard; pooled, the axis is identified (σ1/σ2 = 2.2).

blocks.title: Related work

summary.text: Related work: the game probes the abstraction-and-analogy cluster central to accounts of thinking (Gentner, Hofstadter, Chollet, Mitchell), but where classical analogy tests ask for one keyed selection or completion, it asks for many coupled slots built from scratch and is falsifiable sentence by sentence. As a method it belongs to unsupervised peer evaluation (single judges, PoLL panels, LLM-as-Examiner, PiCO, UPME), differing by weighting agreement only where it can mean truth and by re-contesting its own judges. Also relates the anchor sweep to judge-reliability work on invariance under non-semantic perturbation and to anchor recalibration.

blocks.title: Discussion
blocks.content:
Two yardsticks. The factual estimator’s one assumption — the only thing competent evaluators
share is the truth — is what licenses agreement-weighting for facts. The disclosed alternative applies
it to taste as well (an authority rating, one SVD per subjective axis; Appendix A.7); we decline it
because on taste the dominant axis of agreement is shared convention, so weighting by it would
reward the judge nearest the mean. Peer centrality’s weakness is the shared misunderstanding; rating
consistency asks only whether a judge holds a firm standard.
A sustainable yardstick. When the field outgrow

summary.text: Discussion: peer centrality is used only for facts, because on taste the dominant agreement is shared convention; its weakness is a shared misunderstanding, while consistency only asks for a firm standard. The yardstick is sustainable: when a model beats the anchor by a resolvable margin the anchor is replaced and models re-scored, so the benchmark rises with the models, unlike a keyed test with fixed key-makers. For the 0.98 agreement with GPQA the paper hypothesises both measure knowledge held as archetypal contexts, GPQA instantiating one in one domain and the game one archetype in many, and proposes a falsifiable representation test; the data establish only the correlation.

blocks.title: Limitations
blocks.content:
Steering signal, and its caveat. Self-improvement, the council governing its own rules, is specified
but not exercised. A system optimised against T is optimised against a consensus it participates in,

does not own and independently constituted councils.
Scope. The runs share one configuration — one prompt template, one roster — so the bootstrap
intervals measure item and run-to-run dispersion, not the configuration (the four anchor values give
the

summary.text: Limitations: self-improvement by the council is specified but not exercised, and optimising against a consensus one participates in can reward courting that consensus. All runs share one prompt template and roster, so intervals reflect item and run dispersion rather than configuration; the leading group is at its discrimination floor; no seat has yet been contested; and peer consensus penalises dissent, as a synthetic evaluator inverting a fifth of the consensus verdicts loses most of its competence.

blocks.title: Conclusion
blocks.content:
The metanym game is a structural test of intelligence built entirely of analogy, falsifiable sentence
by sentence. The council-of-peers benchmark needs nothing outside itself: truth as the dominant
axis of inter-evaluator agreement, reliability as invariance under a swept anchor, judges certified by
the participants, contestable seats — and one external check, by design, r = 0.98 against GPQA
Diamond.
AI USE STATEMENT
Every original idea in this work is the author’s. The work was developed in a sustained dialogue with
generative AI assistants (Anthropic’s Claude), directed by the author throug

summary.text: Conclusion, AI-use statement and references: the game is a structural test of intelligence built from analogy, needing nothing external beyond one deliberate check, r = 0.98 against GPQA Diamond. The AI-use statement says the ideas are the author's, developed in dialogue with Anthropic's Claude, which criticised designs, implemented analysis code, cleaned records and drafted text the author rewrote, with no ratings or data generated by AI beyond the twelve rated models. The rest of the block is the reference list.

blocks.title: Rating estimators
blocks.content:
Every rating comes from one object: the scores the participants produce when each model grades
the others’ portfolios, swept across the anchor. No external answer key is used.

folio is graded) and an evaluator (it grades the others). Every model was asked to grade every port-
folio including its own, and those self-evaluations are released; but no rating below uses a model’s
grade of its own portfolio — every estimator is leave-self-out. A portfolio holds five archetypes,
each realised as five

summary.text: Appendix A, rating estimators: all ratings come from the participants' scores of one another's portfolios swept across the anchor, with no external key. blocks.title: The council and the total
blocks.content:
The sweep keeps the anchor interior to the 1–10 scale. At its ends, 5 and 8, the room on one side
of the anchor shrinks, so part of the residual disagreement between anchor values is compression of
the scale rather than reordering; the consistency values are conservative to that extent.
A model is reliable when its competence sits clear of the inert band — its 95% bootstrap interval
on f separates it from the near-zero cluster — and ¯rs ≥0.78. Eight of twelve clear the consistency
gate; five clear both, and that conjunction seats the council. Each evaluator index is rescaled so the
anchor scor

summary.text: Appendix A.4, the council and the total: the sweep keeps the anchor inside the scale, so consistencies are conservative near its ends. A judge is reliable if its competence interval clears the near-zero cluster and its collapsed consistency is at least 0.78; eight pass consistency and five pass both, forming the council. Gives the anchored evaluator scores, the reliability-weighted criterion score GC, and G, E and T as means of the four quarters, with bootstrap intervals that include run-to-run dispersion and are conditional on the selected council.

blocks.title: The contest, the ballast, and the guards
blocks.content:
The official leaderboard is issued on the contest basis: a contest for model c convenes the five
council seats and c itself as evaluators over the incumbents’ portfolios, the two ballast blocks and c’s
own — every estimator above unchanged, leave-self-out throughout, the anchor’s fa, ¯ra the contest’s
own. Two guards decide whether the contest’s factual axis is identified: σ1/σ2 ∈[2.0, 5.0] and a
spread of the seats’ anchored EF above 2.5 points; if either fails, no seat changes hands and the
contest’s totals carry the caveat. The upper bound marks the range within which the sizing below
was v

summary.text: Appendix A.6, the contest, ballast and guards: a contest seats the five council members plus the contestant as evaluators over the incumbents' portfolios, two ballast blocks and the contestant's own, and its factual axis counts as identified only if σ1/σ2 is between 2 and 5 and the seats' EF spread exceeds 2.5 points. Without weak submissions the factual axis breaks, with seats' EF swinging by up to 8.8 points; two fixed ballast blocks of the weakest archived submissions repair it (Table 7). Also sizes the spectral-gap guard against noise, finding run 3 has a shared but not single factual axis that pooling restores.

blocks.title: Authority versus consistency on the subjective axes
blocks.content:
Computed on run 1 alone. Peer centrality can be run on the subjective axes too: one SVD per non-
factual axis yields an authority rating — each judge’s alignment with the participants’ collective
taste. On the five subjective axes authority and consistency correlate at Pearson 0.70–0.90; on factual
— the one axis with a truth to be right about — they diverge (0.50, CI [−0.08, 0.84]), because only
there can a judge be stable yet wrong. Consistency credits a judge’s whole stable standard, personal
taste included, penalising only flimsiness; authority credits the collective share alone, so stable

summary.text: Appendix A.7, authority versus consistency: running peer centrality on the subjective axes gives an 'authority' rating that correlates 0.70–0.90 with consistency there but diverges on the factual axis, where a judge can be stable yet wrong. Council membership is the same under either; substituting authority keeps the ordering (Spearman 0.986) except that Gemini 3.1 Pro overtakes the anchor, but it is rejected because it turns alignment into authority where no truth licenses that. A synthetic consensus-copying judge shows the cost of dissent: EF 5.15, falling to 4.84 with 5% and 3.79 with 20% of verdicts inverted.

blocks.title: The administration, disclosed

summary.text: Appendix D.2, how GPQA was administered: 198 questions on 2026-06-13, two weeks after the generation run, through the same gateway and settings, with only the question and four deterministically shuffled options and an 'Answer: $LETTER' instruction. summary.text: Appendix D.3, the leak audit: a script re-derives the published table from raw records and checks that accuracies reconcile exactly, the key is identical across models and balanced (48/51/47/52, p = 0.95), an independently written extractor agrees except mainly on Gemini's \boxed{} style, and strict terminal-answer rescoring shifts three models slightly with little effect on the correlation. blocks.title: The constructs of intelligence the Metanym Game demands
blocks.content:
Playing the metanym game demands at least eight constructs that cognitive science treats as central
to intelligence, abstraction and analogy above all — one wide cluster, not the whole of it (perception,
motor skill, working memory and social intelligence the Metanym Game leaves alone):
29
Preprint. arXiv:2606.21008 v3, September 2026.
1. Higher-order relational reasoning (Penn et al., 2008) — recognising that two situations
share the same pattern of relations among their parts even when the parts are unrelated.
Each slot is defined by its relations to the other slots, not by its filler word;

summary.text: Appendix E, the constructs of intelligence the game demands: at least eight constructs from cognitive science, centred on abstraction and analogy (not perception, motor skill, working memory or social intelligence), including higher-order relational reasoning, structure-mapping (the metanym table as its bookkeeping), essence-seeing of a novel situation as an instance of a known pattern, and others, ending with collective judgement under shared standards (Longino), which the council mechanises as individual firm standards plus trust flowing to judges trusted by the trusted.
